title: Tree and Graph Assessment
description: Test your understanding of trees, graphs, heaps, and graph traversal algorithms.

questions.question: For a balanced binary search tree with n nodes, what is the average-case time complexity of search, insert, and delete operations?
questions.explanation: A balanced BST keeps its height at O(log n), so search, insert, and delete each take O(log n) on average.

questions.question: Which graph traversal algorithm uses a queue and visits all neighbors at the current depth before moving deeper?
questions.explanation: BFS explores nodes level by level using a queue, which makes it ideal for shortest paths in unweighted graphs.

questions.question: Which data structure allows you to retrieve the maximum or minimum element in O(1) time?
questions.explanation: A heap always exposes its largest (max-heap) or smallest (min-heap) element at the root in O(1) time.

questions.question: A minimum spanning tree of an undirected connected graph connects all vertices using the:
options: Maximum total edge weight with cycles
Minimum total edge weight with no cycles
Exactly the number of edges as vertices squared
questions.explanation: An MST connects every vertex with the smallest possible total edge weight and contains no cycles, using V - 1 edges.

questions.question: For a graph with V vertices and E edges, what is the time complexity of BFS and DFS?
questions.explanation: Both BFS and DFS visit each vertex once and examine each edge once, giving O(V + E).

title: Data Structures Final Assessment
description: Verify your mastery of sorting, searching, and the core data structures from the course.

questions.question: Which comparison-based sorting algorithm guarantees O(n log n) time in all cases but requires O(n) extra space?
questions.explanation: Merge Sort always runs in O(n log n) and merges halves using an auxiliary array, requiring O(n) extra space.

questions.question: Binary search can only be applied to input that is:
questions.explanation: Binary search relies on comparing the middle element and halving the search space, which requires sorted data.

questions.question: What is the average-case time complexity of a hash map lookup?
questions.explanation: Hash maps compute the bucket from the key's hash in constant time, giving O(1) average-case lookups.

questions.question: Which data structure processes elements in First-In, First-Out (FIFO) order?
questions.explanation: A queue inserts at the rear and removes from the front, following FIFO ordering.

questions.question: What is the worst-case time complexity of Quick Sort?
questions.explanation: Quick Sort degrades to O(n²) when the pivot is consistently the smallest or largest element, such as on already sorted input.

title: Python Functions Quiz
description: Check your knowledge of defining and using functions and modules in Python.

questions.question: Which syntax correctly defines a function in Python?
questions.explanation: Python functions are declared with the `def` keyword followed by the function name and parentheses.

questions.question: If a function has no return statement, what does it return by default?
questions.explanation: Functions without an explicit return statement return the special value None.

questions.question: Which keyword is used to import another module in Python?
questions.explanation: The `import` statement brings a module (or names from it) into the current namespace.

questions.question: In a function definition, what does *args allow a function to accept?
options: A variable number of positional arguments as a tuple
questions.explanation: *args collects extra positional arguments into a tuple, letting the function accept any number of them.

questions.question: Lambda functions in Python are:
questions.explanation: A lambda is a small anonymous function defined in a single expression, typically used where a simple callable is needed.

title: Web Development Final Quiz
description: Demonstrate your understanding of HTML, CSS, and JavaScript fundamentals.

questions.question: Which HTML element is the semantic container for the main page heading?
questions.explanation: <h1> is the semantic element for the main document heading; <header> is a container, and <title> sets the browser tab title.

questions.question: CSS Flexbox is primarily designed for:
options: Creating complex grid layouts in two dimensions
Distributing and aligning items along a single axis
questions.explanation: Flexbox lays out items along one axis (row or column); CSS Grid is the two-dimensional layout tool.

questions.question: Which CSS property changes the text color of an element?
questions.explanation: The `color` property sets the foreground text color; background-color affects the element's background.

questions.question: Which CSS unit is relative to the root element's font size?
questions.explanation: `rem` is always relative to the root (<html>) font size, while `em` is relative to the parent element.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the <script> element in an HTML document?
options: To embed or reference executable JavaScript
To add metadata about the page
questions.explanation: The <script> element embeds JavaScript directly or references an external .js file to execute client-side code.

title: Normalization Quiz
description: Test your grasp of normal forms and how they remove redundancy in relational databases.

questions.question: A table is in First Normal Form (1NF) when:
options: Each column holds a single atomic value per row
All non-key columns depend on the full primary key
Every column is a foreign key
questions.explanation: 1NF requires atomic values and no repeating groups, so each cell holds one indivisible value.

questions.question: A table is in Second Normal Form (2NF) when it is in 1NF and:
options: Every non-key attribute fully depends on the entire primary key
The table has a composite primary key
questions.explanation: 2NF removes partial dependencies, meaning every non-key column depends on the whole composite primary key, not part of it.

questions.question: A table is in Third Normal Form (3NF) when it is in 2NF and:
options: There are no transitive dependencies on non-key columns
It has at least three columns
questions.explanation: 3NF eliminates transitive dependencies, where a non-key column depends on another non-key column instead of the key.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a foreign key?
options: To uniquely identify each row in the same table
To reproduce a primary key in another table and enforce relationships
questions.explanation: A foreign key references the primary key of another table, enforcing referential integrity between tables.

questions.question: Which normal form is violated by a table that stores multiple phone numbers in one column?
questions.explanation: Storing multiple values in a single column violates atomicity, so the table is not in 1NF.

title: DBMS Final Assessment
description: Review transactions, SQL, and core database concepts covered throughout the course.

questions.question: What does the ACID acronym stand for in database transactions?
questions.explanation: ACID ensures reliable transactions: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, and Durability.

questions.question: Which SQL clause is used to filter rows after GROUP BY aggregation?
questions.explanation: WHERE filters rows before grouping; HAVING filters groups after aggregation.

questions.question: Which property must a primary key always satisfy?
options: It must be unique and not null
It must be a foreign key
questions.explanation: A primary key uniquely identifies each row, so it must be unique and cannot contain NULL values.

questions.question: Which SQL statement is used to retrieve data from a database?
questions.explanation: SELECT queries and reads data; the others modify or remove data.

questions.question: A deadlock occurs when:
options: Two queries run at the same time
Two transactions each wait for a lock held by the other
questions.explanation: Deadlock happens when concurrent transactions hold locks while waiting for locks the other holds, so neither can proceed.

title: Neural Network Quiz
description: Assess your understanding of how neural networks learn and the role of each layer.

questions.question: Which activation function is most commonly used in the hidden layers of modern neural networks?
questions.explanation: ReLU (Rectified Linear Unit) is fast and helps avoid the vanishing gradient problem in deep networks.

questions.question: Backpropagation is the algorithm used to:
options: Compute gradients to update the network weights
questions.explanation: Backpropagation computes the gradient of the loss with respect to each weight, which gradient descent uses to update them.

questions.question: What does the input layer of a neural network receive?
options: The features of each training example
questions.explanation: The input layer holds the raw feature values that the network transforms in subsequent layers.

questions.question: Overfitting means a model:
options: Performs well on training data but poorly on new data
questions.explanation: An overfit model memorizes noise from training data and generalizes poorly to unseen examples.

questions.question: Which of the following is a supervised learning task?
options: Grouping customers by similarity without labels
Classifying emails as spam or not spam from labeled examples
Reducing dimensions of an image dataset
Finding frequent items in a transaction log
questions.explanation: Classification with labeled examples is supervised learning; the other options are unsupervised or rule-mining tasks.

title: AI Final Assessment
description: Confirm your understanding of ML workflows, evaluation, and real-world AI applications.

questions.question: Why do we split data into training and test sets?
options: To evaluate how well the model generalizes to unseen data
questions.explanation: A held-out test set estimates performance on data the model has never seen, revealing generalization and overfitting.

questions.question: Accuracy is a reliable metric mainly when:
questions.explanation: With balanced classes a high accuracy is meaningful; with skewed data, precision, recall, or F1 are more informative.

questions.question: What is an epoch in machine learning training?
options: One full pass through the entire training dataset
The learning rate multiplied by iterations
questions.explanation: An epoch is completed when the model has seen every training example once.

questions.question: Which of these is a common real-world AI application?
options: Spelling check in a word processor
A recommendation system that personalizes content
A spreadsheet function that sums cells
questions.explanation: Recommendation systems use machine learning models trained on user behavior to personalize suggestions.

questions.question: In supervised learning, model parameters are learned from:
questions.explanation: Parameters are updated during training to minimize loss over the labeled training data.

title: Pivot Table Quiz
description: Check your ability to summarize and analyze data using Excel pivot tables.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of an Excel pivot table?
options: To summarize and aggregate large amounts of tabular data
questions.explanation: Pivot tables let you quickly group, count, and aggregate data across rows and columns without writing formulas.

questions.question: In a pivot table, which area holds the fields you want to sum, count, or average?
questions.explanation: The Values area defines how numeric fields are aggregated, such as Sum, Count, or Average.

questions.question: Which pivot table area determines the fields shown as columns of the summary grid?
questions.explanation: Field names placed in the Columns area become the columns of the aggregated summary.

questions.question: What is a slicer used for in a pivot table?
options: Dividing a column into text pieces
Visually filtering pivot table data by a field's values
questions.explanation: Slicers provide clickable buttons that filter pivot data, and they stay visible and easy to read.

questions.question: After new rows are added to the source data, the pivot table needs to be:
questions.explanation: Pivot tables do not update automatically; use Refresh to pull in the latest source data.

title: Testing Final Quiz
description: Validate your understanding of test types, cases, and automation best practices.

questions.question: What is the main purpose of unit testing?
options: Testing the entire application through the UI
Verifying individual functions or modules in isolation
Load-testing a server with many users
questions.explanation: Unit tests focus on a single unit of code in isolation, catching defects early with fast and focused tests.

questions.question: A well-designed test case should be:
options: Dependent on the order of other tests
questions.explanation: Reliable tests are isolated, produce the same result every run, and can be repeated without external side effects.

questions.question: Boundary value analysis tests:
options: Only the middle value of a range
Values at and near the edges of input ranges
questions.explanation: Bugs often hide at the edges of valid ranges, so BVA tests minimum, maximum, and values just beyond them.

questions.question: What is regression testing used for?
options: Ensuring new changes do not break existing functionality
questions.explanation: Regression tests re-run existing functionality after code changes to catch unintended breaks.

questions.question: Integration testing verifies that:
options: Different modules interact correctly with each other
The UI matches the design mockups
questions.explanation: Integration tests exercise the interaction and contracts between modules, databases, and external services.

title: Java Collections Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of the Java Collections Framework: List, Set, Map, and iterators.

questions.question: Which collection stores unique elements with no guaranteed order?
questions.explanation: HashSet stores unique elements backed by a hash table and offers O(1) average lookup with no ordering guarantees.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of an ArrayList over a LinkedList?
questions.explanation: ArrayList uses a dynamic array, giving O(1) access by index, while LinkedList requires traversal from the head.

questions.question: Which interface is implemented by the HashMap class?
questions.explanation: HashMap implements the Map interface, storing key-value pairs with unique keys.

questions.question: What is the purpose of an Iterator?
options: To convert a collection to a string
To traverse the elements of a collection sequentially
questions.explanation: An iterator lets you step through a collection's elements one by one, supporting standard traversal.

questions.question: To sort a List of custom objects by a chosen attribute, you use:
questions.explanation: Comparable defines the natural order and Comparator allows custom sort keys when sorting lists.

title: Cybersecurity Fundamentals Quiz
description: Apply the cyber defense, cryptography, and audit concepts from the course to real scenarios.

questions.question: The CIA triad stands for:
questions.explanation: Confidentiality, Integrity, and Availability are the three pillars of information security.

questions.question: The principle of least privilege means:
options: Giving all users the same permissions
Giving each user only the permissions needed for their role
questions.explanation: Least privilege limits the blast radius of a compromised account by granting the minimum access required.

questions.question: Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) combines:
options: Two or more different authentication factors
questions.explanation: MFA combines something you know, have, and/or are, so a stolen password alone is not enough to log in.

questions.question: Why are passwords stored as salted hashes instead of plain text?
options: Salted hashes make identical passwords produce different stored values and resist rainbow tables
Plain text is slower to write
questions.explanation: A unique random salt per user prevents identical passwords from having identical hashes and defeats precomputed rainbow tables.

questions.question: During a security audit you find hardcoded API keys in source code. What is the correct first step?
options: Copy the key into the README
Rotate the key and move it to a secrets manager
Ignore it because the repo is private
Share it with the team in chat
questions.explanation: Once a secret appears in code it must be treated as compromised: rotate it immediately and store secrets securely, not in source.
